name: Freed vs Nabla vs Suki AI
title: Freed vs Nabla vs Suki AI: AI Medical Scribe Comparison (2026)
description: Compare Freed, Nabla, and Suki AI for clinical documentation. See differences in pricing, EHR integrations, multilingual support, and which AI scribe is best for your practice.

summary.bottom_line: Freed offers the most affordable entry point at $39/month for budget-conscious solo practitioners. Nabla provides the strongest privacy model (zero server storage) with 35+ language support for diverse patient populations. Suki AI delivers the most comprehensive enterprise solution with voice commands for hands-free EHR navigation and the deepest integrations.

sections.heading: Freed vs Nabla vs Suki AI: Overview
sections.content: Freed, Nabla, and Suki AI represent three distinct approaches to AI medical scribing. Freed targets solo practitioners and small practices with accessible pricing starting at $39/month. Nabla, founded in Paris, differentiates with a privacy-first architecture where patient data never touches their servers and 35+ language support for diverse populations. Suki AI positions as the enterprise solution with $168M in funding, voice commands for hands-free EHR navigation, and deep integrations with Epic, Cerner, and athena. All three use ambient AI to capture patient conversations and generate clinical notes.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Pricing varies dramatically across these three platforms. Freed is most accessible: $39/month Starter (40 notes), $79/month Core (unlimited), $119/month Premier (native EHR push, coding). Nabla no longer publishes pricing but historically charged ~$119/month for individuals and $299-399/month for enterprise. Suki is premium-priced: $299/month for Compose (documentation only) and $399/month for Assistant (full EHR integration and voice commands). For a solo practitioner, annual costs range from $468 (Freed Starter) to $4,788 (Suki Assistant). Freed's 7-day free trial requires no credit card.

sections.heading: Privacy and Data Security
sections.content: Nabla has the strongest privacy model: audio, transcripts, and notes exist only in the clinician's browser and are never stored on Nabla's servers. This is particularly valuable for GDPR compliance and privacy-conscious practices. Freed and Suki use standard encrypted storage models. All three are HIPAA compliant with BAAs available. Freed has SOC 2 Type II certification. Suki has HITRUST certification, which some health systems require. If data privacy is paramount, Nabla's zero-storage architecture is compelling.

sections.heading: EHR Integrations
sections.content: Integration depth varies significantly. Suki has the deepest bi-directional, real-time integration with Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), athenahealth, and MEDITECH Expanse, enabling voice commands to navigate and populate the EHR. Nabla integrates with 20+ EHRs via SMART on FHIR and Nabla Connect, allowing any EHR to embed Nabla in days. Freed works with most EHRs via browser extension (copy-paste) with native push integration on Premier for select systems (Athenahealth, Practice Fusion, SimplePractice, Elation, Tebra). If you need voice-controlled EHR navigation, Suki is the only option.

sections.heading: Multilingual Support
sections.content: All three platforms support multiple languages, but Nabla emphasizes this most strongly with marketing around 35+ languages including Arabic, Mandarin, Spanish, French, Hindi, and Vietnamese. Freed supports 90+ languages for transcription. Suki supports 80+ languages. For practices serving diverse patient populations or international telehealth, multilingual capabilities may be decisive. Nabla's zero-storage model combined with multilingual support makes it particularly attractive for GDPR-compliant international practices.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Match the platform to your practice type and priorities:

recommendations.when: Budget is your primary concern (starting at $39/month), you're a solo practitioner or small practice, you need quick setup with any EHR via browser extension, you want a 7-day free trial without credit card, or you need high-volume affordable documentation (Core at $79/month unlimited)

Data privacy is paramount (zero server storage), you serve diverse patient populations needing multilingual support, you need GDPR compliance for international practice, you want native EHR integration via SMART on FHIR, or you're a mid-market practice willing to pay for privacy guarantees

You're an enterprise or health system, you need voice commands for hands-free EHR navigation, you require HITRUST certification, you use Epic, Cerner, athena, or MEDITECH, or you want the most comprehensive AI assistant beyond just documentation

faqs.q: Which AI scribe is cheapest: Freed, Nabla, or Suki?
faqs.a: Freed is significantly cheaper, starting at $39/month for 40 notes or $79/month for unlimited notes. Nabla starts around $119/month (quote required). Suki starts at $299/month. For budget-conscious solo practitioners, Freed offers the best value.

faqs.q: Which AI scribe has the best privacy protection?
faqs.a: Nabla has the strongest privacy model. Patient audio, transcripts, and notes exist only in the clinician's browser and are never stored on Nabla's servers. This zero-storage architecture provides exceptional privacy guarantees for both HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

faqs.q: Which AI scribe works with Epic?
faqs.a: All three integrate with Epic to varying degrees. Suki has the deepest bi-directional, real-time Epic integration with voice commands. Nabla integrates natively via SMART on FHIR. Freed works with Epic via browser extension and copy-paste. For seamless Epic integration, Suki leads.

faqs.q: Which is best for multilingual patient populations?
faqs.a: Nabla emphasizes multilingual support with 35+ languages including Arabic, Mandarin, Spanish, and Vietnamese. Freed supports 90+ languages for transcription. Suki supports 80+ languages. All three handle non-English speaking patients, but Nabla markets this capability most prominently.

faqs.q: Do these AI scribes work for mental health documentation?
faqs.a: Yes, all three support mental health documentation including therapy progress notes, psychiatric evaluations, and SOAP notes. Freed explicitly lists psychiatry notes among supported types. However, for mental health-specific AI scribes, consider also evaluating Mentalyc or Upheal which specialize in therapy documentation.

faqs.q: Which AI scribe offers voice commands for EHR navigation?
faqs.a: Only Suki AI offers full voice commands for hands-free EHR navigation, ordering, and charting beyond just documentation. This allows clinicians to control their EHR entirely by voice. Freed and Nabla focus on documentation generation rather than EHR control.
